change: ADMIN_READ_KEY: a read-only admin credential an agent can hold without gaining the verify bit
_context: lib/admin-session.js signs the dashboard cookie with ADMIN_KEY itself, so any holder of ADMIN_KEY can mint a valid session offline without calling /admin/login. That cookie is what lib/command-auth.js requireCookieAuth accepts, and it gates POST /api/todo/:id/verify. Handing ADMIN_KEY to an agent therefore hands it the verify bit and retires rule 4 of CLAUDE.md. The first design for this marked sessions as agent-minted at /admin/login and refused the verify bit for those; it was discarded because an ADMIN_KEY holder simply skips /admin/login and signs its own token with browser:true. The boundary has to be a secret the agent does not hold.
_expect_failure_note: Every expect_failure carries the literal [FAIL] prefix, because an assertion NAME also appears on the pass line, so naming it alone would prove only that the assertion ran.

checks.name: the admin API's own suites are unchanged by this
THE ONE THAT MATTERS: the read key must not mint a session
checks._why: If the read key could pass the /admin/login check it would become the full key, because the cookie it receives is signed with ADMIN_KEY and carries every cookie-gated power including the verify bit.
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL]   POST /admin/login with the read key is refused

checks.name: the read key must not be able to write
the read key must not see a student's name
a weak or unset read key must fail closed
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL]   a weak read key is refused

checks.name: the forged-token test must not be hollow
checks._why: The first draft of that assertion read `adminSession.sign ? ... : null` and sign() is not exported, so it passed without ever forging a token. Breaking verify() must now make it go red, which proves it is really forging and really checking.
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL]   a token signed with the read key does not verify

checks.name: production serves this tree
checks._why: Derived from the tree rather than pinned, so it is false before the deploy and false if the deploy never runs.
checks.command: node -e "const cp=require('child_process');const want=cp.execSync('git rev-parse HEAD',{encoding:'utf8'}).trim().slice(0,7);const got=JSON.parse(cp.execSync('curl -sS --max-time 25 https://progress.apcsexamprep.com/api/health',{encoding:'utf8'})).commit;if(got!==want)throw new Error('production serves '+got+', this tree is '+want);console.log('PRODUCTION SERVES THIS TREE '+got);"

_removed_check_note: A mutation for a `read === full` refusal was written and then REMOVED, with the code it targeted. The gate reported that breaking the line left the suite green, which was correct: when the two keys are equal the full-key branch matches first and returns, so the read-only branch is unreachable and the refusal has no observable effect. Keeping a guard no mutation can prove is the hollow-guard failure this repo keeps paying for, so the hazard is documented in routes/admin.js instead of pretended at.
